turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Meredith stops just inside the door and doesn't sit. She sets her bag on the nearest desk.

"Mr. Hale. I have until 4:40." She glances at the clock, then back at you. "My son found out about a zero from a gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. Nobody called me. So before we get to the essay: who decided, and when?"
So the defense is that he just types really fast?

"I haven't offered a defense. I asked who decided, and when." She finally pulls out the chair and sits, but only on the edge of it. "'He just types really fast.' Where did that come from? Is that in a document, or is that your impression?"

She takes a slim folder from her bag and keeps it closed on her knee.

"I'd like to see what you're actually relying on. The checker's report, the date it was run, and anything that shows Owen was asked about it before the zero went in. I'll want that in an email as well."
182 words in six minutes. Wow. Maybe he should be a court stenographer.

"'Wow.' That's an adjective, Mr. Hale. I'm asking for a source."

She opens the folder now and uncaps a pen.

"182 words in six minutes. Where is that number from? The version history? Which document, which dates, and who pulled it? And is it one stretch out of the whole essay, or is it the whole essay?" She looks up. "Because a six-minute window isn't an essay. Did the history show that he wrote it over the weekend, or didn't it?"

A beat.

"And 'maybe he should be a court stenographer.' Is that going in the file? Because I'd want to know what else is."

"I'm not counsel in this room. I'm his mother." Her pen stops. "But 'counsel' tells me you think this is a fight. Is it?"

She doesn't raise her voice.

"I haven't offered a theory. I've asked four questions, and you've answered none of them. What's the source for the 182 words? Who ran the checker, and when? Was Owen asked anything before the zero went in?"

She sets the pen down on the folder.

"If you have a document, show me. If you don't, say so, and we'll talk about that instead."
